about: MySQL 8.4 and MariaDB 11 built-ins beyond common.json. Entries marked (MySQL only) or (MariaDB only) exist in just one engine. Function names are UPPERCASE.

functions.name: COUNT
functions.summary: Counts rows (COUNT(*)), non-NULL values of an expression, or distinct non-NULL combinations of one or more expressions.

params.name: * | expression
params.doc: * counts every row; an expression counts rows where it is not NULL.

params.name: DISTINCT expression
params.doc: Counts distinct non-NULL values; MySQL accepts several expressions and counts distinct combinations.

functions.name: GROUP_CONCAT
functions.summary: Concatenates the non-NULL values of a group into one string, optionally distinct, ordered and with a custom separator (default ','). The result is truncated to group_concat_max_len bytes.
functions.example: GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT name ORDER BY name SEPARATOR ', ')

params.name: [DISTINCT] expr [, …] [ORDER BY …] [SEPARATOR str]
params.doc: The values to join, optionally DISTINCT, followed by an ORDER BY list and a SEPARATOR string.

functions.name: JSON_ARRAYAGG
functions.summary: Aggregates a group's values, including NULLs, into a JSON array.

params.name: expression
params.doc: The value added to the array for each row.

functions.name: JSON_OBJECTAGG
functions.summary: Aggregates key/value pairs from a group into a JSON object; with duplicate keys the last value wins.

params.name: key
params.doc: The member name; must not be NULL.

functions.name: BIT_AND
functions.summary: Returns the bitwise AND of all values in the group.

params.name: expression
params.doc: The values to combine bit by bit.

functions.name: BIT_OR
functions.summary: Returns the bitwise OR of all values in the group.

params.name: expression
params.doc: The values to combine bit by bit.

functions.name: BIT_XOR
functions.summary: Returns the bitwise XOR of all values in the group.

params.name: expression
params.doc: The values to combine bit by bit.

functions.name: STD
functions.summary: Returns the population standard deviation of the group; a synonym for STDDEV_POP.

functions.name: STDDEV
functions.summary: Returns the population standard deviation of the group; a synonym for STDDEV_POP.

functions.name: STDDEV_POP
functions.summary: Returns the population standard deviation of the group.

functions.name: STDDEV_SAMP
functions.summary: Returns the sample standard deviation of the group.

functions.name: VAR_POP
functions.summary: Returns the population variance of the group.

functions.name: VAR_SAMP
functions.summary: Returns the sample variance of the group.

functions.name: VARIANCE
functions.summary: Returns the population variance of the group; a synonym for VAR_POP.

functions.name: ANY_VALUE
functions.summary: Returns an arbitrary value from the group, suppressing the ONLY_FULL_GROUP_BY error for a column that is not grouped. (MySQL only)

params.name: expression
params.doc: The value to pick from the group.

functions.name: GROUPING
functions.summary: Returns 1 when the column is a super-aggregate NULL produced by WITH ROLLUP, else 0; several arguments return a bitmask. (MySQL only)

functions.name: MEDIAN
functions.summary: Returns the median of the values in the window partition; used with OVER (PARTITION BY …). (MariaDB only)

functions.name: PERCENTILE_CONT
functions.summary: Returns the interpolated value at a fraction of the ordered values: PERCENTILE_CONT(f) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY x) OVER (…). (MariaDB only)
functions.example: PERCENTILE_CONT(0.5) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY salary) OVER (PARTITION BY dept)

params.name: fraction
params.doc: The percentile to compute, between 0 and 1.

functions.name: PERCENTILE_DISC
functions.summary: Returns the first ordered value whose cumulative distribution reaches the fraction: PERCENTILE_DISC(f) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY x) OVER (…). (MariaDB only)
functions.example: PERCENTILE_DISC(0.9) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY latency) OVER ()

signatures.returns: same type as the ORDER BY expression

params.name: fraction
params.doc: The percentile to compute, between 0 and 1.

functions.name: NTH_VALUE
functions.summary: Returns the value of the expression from the N-th row of the window frame, or NULL if there is no such row.

params.name: N
params.doc: The 1-based row within the frame; may be followed by FROM FIRST and RESPECT NULLS.

functions.name: IF
functions.summary: Returns the second argument when the condition is true (not zero and not NULL), otherwise the third.

signatures.returns: common type of the two results

params.name: value_if_true
params.doc: Returned when the condition is true.

params.name: value_if_false
params.doc: Returned when the condition is false or NULL.

functions.name: IFNULL
functions.summary: Returns the first argument if it is not NULL, otherwise the second.

functions.name: NVL
functions.summary: Returns the first argument if it is not NULL, otherwise the second; a synonym for IFNULL. (MariaDB only)

functions.name: NVL2
functions.summary: Returns the second argument when the first is not NULL, otherwise the third. (MariaDB only)

params.name: expr1
params.doc: The value to test for NULL.

params.name: expr2
params.doc: Returned when expr1 is not NULL.

functions.name: ISNULL
functions.summary: Returns 1 if the argument is NULL, otherwise 0.

functions.name: GREATEST
functions.summary: Returns the largest argument; returns NULL if any argument is NULL.

params.name: value
params.doc: A value to compare; at least two are required.

functions.name: LEAST
functions.summary: Returns the smallest argument; returns NULL if any argument is NULL.

params.name: value
params.doc: A value to compare; at least two are required.

functions.name: LENGTH
functions.summary: Returns the length of a string in bytes (a multibyte character counts as several bytes).

functions.name: OCTET_LENGTH
functions.summary: Returns the length of a string in bytes; a synonym for LENGTH.

functions.name: LENGTHB
functions.summary: Returns the length of a string in bytes; a synonym for LENGTH. (MariaDB only)

functions.name: CHAR_LENGTH
functions.summary: Returns the length of a string in characters.

functions.name: CHARACTER_LENGTH
functions.summary: Returns the length of a string in characters; a synonym for CHAR_LENGTH.

functions.name: BIT_LENGTH
functions.summary: Returns the length of a string in bits.

functions.name: CONCAT
functions.summary: Concatenates the arguments into one string; returns NULL if any argument is NULL.

params.name: str
params.doc: A value to append; numbers are converted to strings.

functions.name: CONCAT_WS
functions.summary: Concatenates the arguments with a separator between them, skipping NULL arguments.

params.name: separator
params.doc: Placed between each pair of values; a NULL separator gives NULL.

params.name: str
params.doc: A value to join; NULLs are skipped.

functions.name: SUBSTRING
functions.summary: Returns part of a string starting at a position, optionally limited to a length.

params.name: pos
params.doc: 1-based start position; negative counts from the end.

params.name: len
params.doc: How many characters to return; the default is to the end.

params.name: str FROM pos [FOR len]
params.doc: Standard SQL form: the string, then FROM start position and optional FOR length.

functions.name: SUBSTR
functions.summary: Returns part of a string starting at a position; a synonym for SUBSTRING.

params.name: pos
params.doc: 1-based start position; negative counts from the end.

params.name: len
params.doc: How many characters to return; the default is to the end.

params.name: str FROM pos [FOR len]
params.doc: Standard SQL form: the string, then FROM start position and optional FOR length.

functions.name: MID
functions.summary: Returns part of a string starting at a position; a synonym for SUBSTRING(str, pos, len).

params.name: pos
params.doc: 1-based start position; negative counts from the end.

functions.name: SUBSTRING_INDEX
functions.summary: Returns the part of a string before the count-th occurrence of a delimiter (from the left), or after it counting from the right when count is negative.

params.name: delim
params.doc: The delimiter to search for; matched case-sensitively.

params.name: count
params.doc: Which occurrence; positive counts from the left, negative from the right.

functions.name: LEFT
functions.summary: Returns the leftmost len characters of a string.

functions.name: RIGHT
functions.summary: Returns the rightmost len characters of a string.

functions.name: LPAD
functions.summary: Left-pads a string with another string to a total length, or truncates it to that length.

params.name: len
params.doc: The length of the result in characters.

params.name: padstr
params.doc: The padding string; optional in MariaDB, where it defaults to a space.

functions.name: RPAD
functions.summary: Right-pads a string with another string to a total length, or truncates it to that length.

params.name: len
params.doc: The length of the result in characters.

params.name: padstr
params.doc: The padding string; optional in MariaDB, where it defaults to a space.

functions.name: INSTR
functions.summary: Returns the 1-based position of the first occurrence of a substring, or 0 if not found. Note the argument order: string first.

functions.name: LOCATE
functions.summary: Returns the 1-based position of the first occurrence of a substring, optionally starting at a position; 0 if not found.

params.name: pos
params.doc: The position to start searching from.

functions.name: POSITION
functions.summary: Returns the 1-based position of the first occurrence of a substring, or 0 if not found; a synonym for LOCATE(substr, str).

params.name: substr IN str
params.doc: The substring, the keyword IN, then the string to search.

functions.name: REPEAT
functions.summary: Returns a string repeated count times; an empty string if count is less than 1.

functions.name: REVERSE
functions.summary: Returns the string with its characters in reverse order.

functions.name: INSERT
functions.summary: Returns the string with the substring starting at pos and len characters long replaced by newstr.

functions.name: FIELD
functions.summary: Returns the 1-based index of the first argument within the rest of the list, or 0 if not found. Often used in ORDER BY for a custom order.

functions.name: FIND_IN_SET
functions.summary: Returns the 1-based position of a string within a comma-separated list, or 0 if not found.

params.name: str
params.doc: The value to look for; must not contain a comma.

functions.name: ELT
functions.summary: Returns the N-th string from the list, or NULL if N is out of range.

params.name: N
params.doc: 1-based index of the string to return.

functions.name: MAKE_SET
functions.summary: Returns a comma-separated list of the strings whose bits are set in the bitmask.

params.name: bits
params.doc: The bitmask; bit 0 selects the first string.

params.name: str
params.doc: A string selected by the next bit.

functions.name: EXPORT_SET
functions.summary: Returns a string with an on string for every set bit and an off string for every clear bit, checked from the lowest bit.

params.name: separator
params.doc: Placed between items; the default is ','.

params.name: number_of_bits
params.doc: How many bits to examine; the default and maximum is 64.

functions.name: FORMAT
functions.summary: Formats a number like '#,###,###.##' rounded to D decimal places, using a locale for separators.

params.name: locale
params.doc: A locale such as 'de_DE' for separators; the default is 'en_US'.

functions.name: SFORMAT
functions.summary: Formats a string using fmt-library style {} placeholders filled from the remaining arguments. (MariaDB only)

params.name: value
params.doc: A value for the next placeholder.

functions.name: HEX
functions.summary: Returns the hexadecimal representation of a number or of each byte of a string.

params.name: N_or_str
params.doc: A number (converted as BIGINT) or a string (each byte becomes two hex digits).

functions.name: UNHEX
functions.summary: Converts pairs of hexadecimal digits to the bytes they represent; returns NULL for invalid digits.

functions.name: LCASE
functions.summary: Returns the string in lowercase; a synonym for LOWER.

functions.name: UCASE
functions.summary: Returns the string in uppercase; a synonym for UPPER.

functions.name: TRIM
functions.summary: Removes leading and/or trailing occurrences of a string (spaces by default) from a string.

params.name: [BOTH | LEADING | TRAILING] [remstr] FROM str
params.doc: Which side to trim (BOTH by default), the text to remove (a space by default), FROM, then the string.

functions.name: SPACE
functions.summary: Returns a string of N spaces.

functions.name: STRCMP
functions.summary: Compares two strings using the collation: returns 0 if equal, -1 if the first sorts first, 1 otherwise.

functions.name: SOUNDEX
functions.summary: Returns the Soundex code of a string, so words that sound alike get the same code.

functions.name: QUOTE
functions.summary: Quotes a string for use as a SQL string literal, escaping quotes, backslashes, NUL and Ctrl-Z; NULL gives the word NULL.

functions.name: ASCII
functions.summary: Returns the numeric value of the first byte of a string; 0 for an empty string.

functions.name: ORD
functions.summary: Returns the code of the first character of a string, combining the bytes of a multibyte character.

functions.name: CHAR
functions.summary: Returns the string made of the characters with the given integer codes, as a binary string unless USING charset is given.

params.name: N
params.doc: A character code; after the last one you may add USING charset_name.

functions.name: CHR
functions.summary: Returns the character with the given code in the connection character set. (MariaDB only)

functions.name: BIN
functions.summary: Returns the binary (base 2) representation of a BIGINT as a string.

functions.name: OCT
functions.summary: Returns the octal (base 8) representation of a BIGINT as a string.

functions.name: CONV
functions.summary: Converts a number from one base to another, bases 2 to 36; a negative to_base treats the value as signed.

params.name: N
params.doc: The value to convert, as a number or a string of digits.

functions.name: REGEXP_LIKE
functions.summary: Returns 1 if the string matches the regular expression, 0 if not. (MySQL only; MariaDB uses the REGEXP operator)

params.name: match_type
params.doc: Flags: 'c' case-sensitive, 'i' case-insensitive, 'm' multiline, 'n' dot matches newline, 'u' Unix line endings.

functions.name: REGEXP_REPLACE
functions.summary: Replaces occurrences of a regular expression in a string. MariaDB accepts only the first three arguments.

params.name: pos
params.doc: Position to start searching from; the default is 1. (MySQL only)

params.name: occurrence
params.doc: Which match to replace; 0 (the default) replaces all. (MySQL only)

params.name: match_type
params.doc: Matching flags such as 'c' or 'i'. (MySQL only)

functions.name: REGEXP_INSTR
functions.summary: Returns the position of a regular expression match in a string, or 0. MariaDB accepts only the first two arguments.

params.name: pos
params.doc: Position to start searching from. (MySQL only)

params.name: occurrence
params.doc: Which match to find; the default is 1. (MySQL only)

params.name: return_option
params.doc: 0 returns the match start (default), 1 the position after it. (MySQL only)

params.name: match_type
params.doc: Matching flags such as 'c' or 'i'. (MySQL only)

functions.name: REGEXP_SUBSTR
functions.summary: Returns the substring that matches a regular expression, or NULL. MariaDB accepts only the first two arguments.

params.name: pos
params.doc: Position to start searching from. (MySQL only)

params.name: occurrence
params.doc: Which match to return; the default is 1. (MySQL only)

params.name: match_type
params.doc: Matching flags such as 'c' or 'i'. (MySQL only)

functions.name: TO_BASE64
functions.summary: Encodes a string as base-64 text.

functions.name: FROM_BASE64
functions.summary: Decodes base-64 text and returns the binary string; NULL for invalid input.

functions.name: WEIGHT_STRING
functions.summary: Returns the collation weight string of a string, the binary value used for comparing and sorting it.

params.name: str [AS CHAR(N) | AS BINARY(N)]
params.doc: The string, optionally cast to a fixed length first.

functions.name: LOAD_FILE
functions.summary: Reads a file on the server host and returns its contents; needs the FILE privilege and respects secure_file_priv.

params.name: file_name
params.doc: Full path of the file on the server.

functions.name: NATURAL_SORT_KEY
functions.summary: Returns a sort key that orders strings with embedded numbers naturally ('a2' before 'a10'). (MariaDB only)

functions.name: TO_CHAR
functions.summary: Converts a date or number to a string using an Oracle-style format such as 'YYYY-MM-DD HH24:MI:SS'. (MariaDB only)

functions.name: CEIL
functions.summary: Returns the smallest integer not less than X; a synonym for CEILING.

functions.name: CEILING
functions.summary: Returns the smallest integer not less than X.

functions.name: FLOOR
functions.summary: Returns the largest integer not greater than X.

functions.name: TRUNCATE
functions.summary: Returns X truncated (not rounded) to D decimal places; a negative D zeroes digits left of the point.

params.name: D
params.doc: The number of decimal places to keep.

functions.name: MOD
functions.summary: Returns the remainder of N divided by M; the same as N % M or N MOD M. NULL when M is 0.

functions.name: POW
functions.summary: Returns X raised to the power Y.

functions.name: POWER
functions.summary: Returns X raised to the power Y; a synonym for POW.

functions.name: SQRT
functions.summary: Returns the square root of a non-negative number; NULL for a negative one.

functions.name: EXP
functions.summary: Returns e raised to the power X.

functions.name: LN
functions.summary: Returns the natural logarithm of X; NULL when X is 0 or less.

functions.name: LOG
functions.summary: With one argument returns the natural logarithm of X; with two returns the logarithm of X to base B.

params.name: X
params.doc: The value; must be greater than 0.

params.name: X
params.doc: The value; must be greater than 0.

functions.name: LOG2
functions.summary: Returns the base-2 logarithm of X.

functions.name: LOG10
functions.summary: Returns the base-10 logarithm of X.

functions.name: PI
functions.summary: Returns the value of pi (3.141593 displayed; full double precision internally).

functions.name: RAND
functions.summary: Returns a random floating-point value v with 0 <= v < 1; a seed makes the sequence repeatable.

params.name: N
params.doc: Seed value for a repeatable sequence.

functions.name: SIGN
functions.summary: Returns -1, 0 or 1 depending on whether X is negative, zero or positive.

functions.name: SIN
functions.summary: Returns the sine of X, where X is in radians.

functions.name: COS
functions.summary: Returns the cosine of X, where X is in radians.

functions.name: TAN
functions.summary: Returns the tangent of X, where X is in radians.

functions.name: COT
functions.summary: Returns the cotangent of X, where X is in radians.

functions.name: ASIN
functions.summary: Returns the arc sine of X in radians; NULL if X is outside -1 to 1.

functions.name: ACOS
functions.summary: Returns the arc cosine of X in radians; NULL if X is outside -1 to 1.

functions.name: ATAN
functions.summary: Returns the arc tangent of X in radians; with two arguments returns the arc tangent of Y/X using both signs to pick the quadrant.

functions.name: ATAN2
functions.summary: Returns the arc tangent of Y/X in radians, using the signs of both to determine the quadrant.

functions.name: DEGREES
functions.summary: Converts X from radians to degrees.

functions.name: RADIANS
functions.summary: Converts X from degrees to radians.

functions.name: CRC32
functions.summary: Returns the CRC-32 checksum of a string as an unsigned 32-bit integer.

functions.name: CRC32C
functions.summary: Returns the CRC-32C (Castagnoli) checksum of a string; an optional first argument continues a previous checksum. (MariaDB only)

params.name: par
params.doc: A previous checksum to continue from.

functions.name: BIT_COUNT
functions.summary: Returns the number of bits that are set in the argument.

params.name: N
params.doc: The value whose 1 bits are counted.

functions.name: NOW
functions.summary: Returns the date and time at which the statement began, in the session time zone.

params.name: fsp
params.doc: Fractional seconds precision, 0 to 6; the default is 0.

functions.name: SYSDATE
functions.summary: Returns the date and time at which the function executes, unlike NOW, which is fixed for the statement.

params.name: fsp
params.doc: Fractional seconds precision, 0 to 6; the default is 0.

functions.name: CURDATE
functions.summary: Returns the current date.

functions.name: CURRENT_DATE
functions.summary: Returns the current date; a synonym for CURDATE().

functions.name: CURTIME
functions.summary: Returns the current time.

params.name: fsp
params.doc: Fractional seconds precision, 0 to 6; the default is 0.

functions.name: CURRENT_TIME
functions.summary: Returns the current time; a synonym for CURTIME().

params.name: fsp
params.doc: Fractional seconds precision, 0 to 6; the default is 0.

functions.name: CURRENT_TIMESTAMP
functions.summary: Returns the date and time at which the statement began; a synonym for NOW(). Also allowed as a column DEFAULT and ON UPDATE value.

params.name: fsp
params.doc: Fractional seconds precision, 0 to 6; the default is 0.

functions.name: LOCALTIME
functions.summary: Returns the current date and time; a synonym for NOW().

params.name: fsp
params.doc: Fractional seconds precision, 0 to 6; the default is 0.

functions.name: LOCALTIMESTAMP
functions.summary: Returns the current date and time; a synonym for NOW().

params.name: fsp
params.doc: Fractional seconds precision, 0 to 6; the default is 0.

functions.name: UTC_DATE
functions.summary: Returns the current UTC date.

functions.name: UTC_TIME
functions.summary: Returns the current UTC time.

params.name: fsp
params.doc: Fractional seconds precision, 0 to 6; the default is 0.

functions.name: UTC_TIMESTAMP
functions.summary: Returns the current UTC date and time.

params.name: fsp
params.doc: Fractional seconds precision, 0 to 6; the default is 0.

functions.name: UNIX_TIMESTAMP
functions.summary: Returns seconds since 1970-01-01 00:00:00 UTC for now or for the given date, interpreted in the session time zone.

params.name: date
params.doc: A date, datetime or timestamp; the default is now.

functions.name: FROM_UNIXTIME
functions.summary: Converts a Unix timestamp to a datetime in the session time zone, optionally formatted like DATE_FORMAT.

params.name: unix_timestamp
params.doc: Seconds since the Unix epoch; may have a fractional part.

functions.name: DATE
functions.summary: Extracts the date part of a date or datetime expression.

functions.name: TIME
functions.summary: Extracts the time part of a time or datetime expression.

functions.name: TIMESTAMP
functions.summary: Returns a datetime from a date or datetime; with a second argument adds that time to it.

functions.name: DATE_ADD
functions.summary: Adds an interval to a date or datetime and returns the result.

params.name: INTERVAL expr unit
params.doc: The keyword INTERVAL, an amount (negative subtracts) and a unit such as DAY, MONTH or HOUR_MINUTE.

functions.name: DATE_SUB
functions.summary: Subtracts an interval from a date or datetime and returns the result.

params.name: INTERVAL expr unit
params.doc: The keyword INTERVAL, an amount and a unit such as DAY, MONTH or HOUR_MINUTE.

functions.name: ADDDATE
functions.summary: Adds an interval to a date; with a plain number as the second argument adds that many days.

params.name: INTERVAL expr unit
params.doc: The keyword INTERVAL, an amount and a unit such as DAY or MONTH.

params.name: days
params.doc: The number of days to add.

functions.name: SUBDATE
functions.summary: Subtracts an interval from a date; with a plain number as the second argument subtracts that many days.

params.name: INTERVAL expr unit
params.doc: The keyword INTERVAL, an amount and a unit such as DAY or MONTH.

params.name: days
params.doc: The number of days to subtract.

functions.name: ADDTIME
functions.summary: Adds a time value to a time or datetime value.

params.name: expr2
params.doc: The time to add, such as '01:30:00'.

functions.name: SUBTIME
functions.summary: Subtracts a time value from a time or datetime value.

functions.name: DATEDIFF
functions.summary: Returns the number of days from expr2 to expr1 (expr1 - expr2), ignoring time parts.

functions.name: TIMEDIFF
functions.summary: Returns expr1 - expr2 as a time value; both must be the same type (both TIME or both DATETIME).

functions.name: TIMESTAMPDIFF
functions.summary: Returns datetime_expr2 - datetime_expr1 as a whole number of the given unit.

params.name: unit
params.doc: The unit of the result, such as DAY, MONTH or SECOND.

functions.name: TIMESTAMPADD
functions.summary: Adds an integer number of units to a date or datetime.

params.name: unit
params.doc: The unit of the interval, such as DAY, MONTH or SECOND.

params.name: interval
params.doc: How many units to add; negative subtracts.

functions.name: EXTRACT
functions.summary: Extracts a part, or a combination of parts such as DAY_HOUR, from a date or time value.

params.name: unit FROM date
params.doc: The unit to extract, the keyword FROM, then the date or time value.

functions.name: DATE_FORMAT
functions.summary: Formats a date or datetime as a string using % format specifiers.

params.name: format
params.doc: The format, with specifiers such as %Y year, %m month, %d day, %H hour, %i minutes, %s seconds.

params.name: locale
params.doc: Locale for month and day names, such as 'de_DE'. (MariaDB only)

functions.name: TIME_FORMAT
functions.summary: Formats a time value as a string; only hour, minute, second and microsecond specifiers apply.

functions.name: STR_TO_DATE
functions.summary: Parses a string into a DATE, TIME or DATETIME using DATE_FORMAT specifiers; NULL if it does not match.

params.name: format
params.doc: The format, with specifiers such as %Y year, %m month, %d day, %H hour, %i minutes, %s seconds.

functions.name: GET_FORMAT
functions.summary: Returns a DATE_FORMAT format string for a type and a standard: 'EUR', 'USA', 'JIS', 'ISO' or 'INTERNAL'.

params.name: type
params.doc: The kind of value to format.

functions.name: DAYNAME
functions.summary: Returns the name of the weekday, such as 'Monday', in the lc_time_names locale.

functions.name: DAYOFMONTH
functions.summary: Returns the day of the month, 1 to 31 (0 for dates like '0000-00-00').

functions.name: DAY
functions.summary: Returns the day of the month, 1 to 31; a synonym for DAYOFMONTH.

functions.name: DAYOFWEEK
functions.summary: Returns the weekday index, 1 = Sunday through 7 = Saturday (ODBC standard).

functions.name: DAYOFYEAR
functions.summary: Returns the day of the year, 1 to 366.

functions.name: WEEKDAY
functions.summary: Returns the weekday index, 0 = Monday through 6 = Sunday.

functions.name: MONTH
functions.summary: Returns the month, 1 to 12.

functions.name: MONTHNAME
functions.summary: Returns the name of the month, such as 'January', in the lc_time_names locale.

functions.name: YEAR
functions.summary: Returns the year, 1000 to 9999.

functions.name: QUARTER
functions.summary: Returns the quarter of the year, 1 to 4.

functions.name: WEEKOFYEAR
functions.summary: Returns the calendar week of the date, 1 to 53; the same as WEEK(date, 3).

functions.name: HOUR
functions.summary: Returns the hour of a time value; can exceed 23 for TIME values.

functions.name: MINUTE
functions.summary: Returns the minute, 0 to 59.

functions.name: SECOND
functions.summary: Returns the second, 0 to 59.

functions.name: MICROSECOND
functions.summary: Returns the microseconds, 0 to 999999.

functions.name: LAST_DAY
functions.summary: Returns the last day of the month of the given date.

functions.name: TO_DAYS
functions.summary: Returns the day number of a date: days since year 0.

functions.name: TO_SECONDS
functions.summary: Returns the number of seconds since year 0 for a date or datetime.

functions.name: TIME_TO_SEC
functions.summary: Returns a time value converted to seconds.

functions.name: WEEK
functions.summary: Returns the week number of a date, 0 to 53 or 1 to 53 depending on mode.

params.name: mode
params.doc: 0 to 7: whether weeks start on Sunday or Monday and how week 1 is chosen; the default comes from default_week_format.

functions.name: YEARWEEK
functions.summary: Returns year and week for a date as a number such as 202452; the year may differ from the date's year at year boundaries.

params.name: mode
params.doc: 0 to 7: whether weeks start on Sunday or Monday and how week 1 is chosen; the default comes from default_week_format.

functions.name: MAKEDATE
functions.summary: Returns a date from a year and a day-of-year number; NULL if dayofyear is less than 1.

params.name: dayofyear
params.doc: The day of the year, starting at 1; larger values roll into later years.

functions.name: MAKETIME
functions.summary: Returns a time value built from hours, minutes and seconds.

params.name: second
params.doc: The seconds, may have a fraction.

functions.name: PERIOD_ADD
functions.summary: Adds N months to a period in YYMM or YYYYMM format and returns a YYYYMM number.

params.name: N
params.doc: The number of months to add.

functions.name: PERIOD_DIFF
functions.summary: Returns the number of months between two periods in YYMM or YYYYMM format.

functions.name: FROM_DAYS
functions.summary: Returns the date for a day number (the inverse of TO_DAYS).

functions.name: SEC_TO_TIME
functions.summary: Converts a number of seconds to a TIME value.

functions.name: CONVERT_TZ
functions.summary: Converts a datetime from one time zone to another; named zones need the time zone tables loaded.

params.name: from_tz
params.doc: The source zone, such as '+00:00' or 'UTC'.

params.name: to_tz
params.doc: The target zone, such as '-05:00' or 'America/New_York'.

functions.name: ADD_MONTHS
functions.summary: Adds a number of months to a date. (MariaDB only)

params.name: months
params.doc: The number of months to add; negative subtracts.

functions.name: CAST
functions.summary: Converts a value to another type. MySQL's target types are limited to BINARY, CHAR, DATE, DATETIME, DECIMAL, DOUBLE, FLOAT, JSON, NCHAR, REAL, SIGNED, UNSIGNED, TIME and YEAR (not INT or VARCHAR).

params.name: expression AS type
params.doc: The value, AS, then a target such as CHAR(10), SIGNED, UNSIGNED, DECIMAL(10,2), DATE, DATETIME(3) or JSON.

functions.name: CONVERT
functions.summary: Converts a value to another type, like CAST, or with USING converts a string to another character set.

params.name: type
params.doc: The target type, such as CHAR, SIGNED, UNSIGNED, DECIMAL(10,2), DATE or DATETIME.

params.name: expression USING charset
params.doc: The string, USING, then a character set such as utf8mb4 or latin1.

functions.name: JSON_OBJECT
functions.summary: Builds a JSON object from alternating key and value arguments.

params.name: value
params.doc: The member value; key/value pairs repeat.

functions.name: JSON_ARRAY
functions.summary: Builds a JSON array from the arguments.

functions.name: JSON_EXTRACT
functions.summary: Returns the data at one or more paths of a JSON document; col->'$.path' is shorthand. Several paths give an array.

params.name: path
params.doc: A JSON path expression such as '$.a[0]'.

functions.name: JSON_UNQUOTE
functions.summary: Removes the quotes from a JSON string value and returns it as text; col->>'$.path' is shorthand for extract plus unquote.

functions.name: JSON_SET
functions.summary: Inserts or replaces values at paths in a JSON document and returns the result.

params.name: path
params.doc: A JSON path expression such as '$.a[0]'.

params.name: val
params.doc: The value for that path; path/value pairs repeat.

functions.name: JSON_INSERT
functions.summary: Inserts values at paths that do not exist yet in a JSON document; existing values are left alone.

params.name: path
params.doc: A JSON path expression such as '$.a[0]'.

params.name: val
params.doc: The value for that path; path/value pairs repeat.

functions.name: JSON_REPLACE
functions.summary: Replaces values at paths that already exist in a JSON document; missing paths are ignored.

params.name: path
params.doc: A JSON path expression such as '$.a[0]'.

params.name: val
params.doc: The value for that path; path/value pairs repeat.

functions.name: JSON_ARRAY_APPEND
functions.summary: Appends values to the end of the arrays at the given paths of a JSON document.

params.name: path
params.doc: A JSON path expression such as '$.a[0]'.

params.name: val
params.doc: The value for that path; path/value pairs repeat.

functions.name: JSON_ARRAY_INSERT
functions.summary: Inserts values into arrays at the given path positions, shifting later elements.

params.name: path
params.doc: A JSON path expression such as '$.a[0]'.

params.name: val
params.doc: The value for that path; path/value pairs repeat.

functions.name: JSON_REMOVE
functions.summary: Removes the data at one or more paths from a JSON document.

params.name: path
params.doc: A JSON path expression such as '$.a[0]'.

functions.name: JSON_CONTAINS
functions.summary: Returns 1 if a JSON document contains a candidate value, optionally at a path; 0 if not.

params.name: candidate
params.doc: The JSON value to look for.

params.name: path
params.doc: Limit the search to this path.

functions.name: JSON_CONTAINS_PATH
functions.summary: Returns 1 if a JSON document has data at one ('one') or all ('all') of the given paths.

params.name: one_or_all
params.doc: 'one' to need any path, 'all' to need every path.

params.name: path
params.doc: A JSON path expression such as '$.a[0]'.

functions.name: JSON_KEYS
functions.summary: Returns the top-level keys of a JSON object, or of the object at a path, as a JSON array.

params.name: path
params.doc: The object whose keys to list.

functions.name: JSON_LENGTH
functions.summary: Returns the number of elements of an array, members of an object, or 1 for a scalar, optionally at a path.

functions.name: JSON_TYPE
functions.summary: Returns the type of a JSON value as a string such as OBJECT, ARRAY, STRING, INTEGER or NULL.

functions.name: JSON_VALID
functions.summary: Returns 1 if the value is valid JSON, otherwise 0.

functions.name: JSON_DEPTH
functions.summary: Returns the maximum nesting depth of a JSON document; a scalar or empty container has depth 1.

functions.name: JSON_MERGE_PATCH
functions.summary: Merges JSON documents following RFC 7396: later members replace earlier ones and null values remove members.

params.name: json_doc2
params.doc: The next document to merge in.

functions.name: JSON_MERGE_PRESERVE
functions.summary: Merges JSON documents, keeping every value: duplicate keys and arrays are combined into arrays.

params.name: json_doc2
params.doc: The next document to merge in.

functions.name: JSON_SEARCH
functions.summary: Returns the path to a matching string in a JSON document ('one') or an array of all paths ('all'); LIKE wildcards apply.

params.name: one_or_all
params.doc: 'one' for the first match, 'all' for every match.

params.name: search_str
params.doc: The string to find; % and _ are wildcards.

params.name: escape_char
params.doc: Escape character for wildcards; NULL means backslash.

params.name: path
params.doc: Limit the search to these paths.

functions.name: JSON_TABLE
functions.summary: Turns JSON data into a relational table in the FROM clause: JSON_TABLE(doc, path COLUMNS (…)) AS alias.
functions.example: JSON_TABLE(doc, '$[*]' COLUMNS (id INT PATH '$.id')) AS jt

params.name: path COLUMNS (column_list)
params.doc: The row path, then COLUMNS with definitions like name VARCHAR(40) PATH '$.name' or id FOR ORDINALITY.

functions.name: JSON_VALUE
functions.summary: Extracts a scalar at a path. MySQL also accepts RETURNING type and ON EMPTY / ON ERROR clauses after the path.

params.name: path [RETURNING type] [on_empty] [on_error]
params.doc: The path, optionally followed by RETURNING type and NULL/ERROR/DEFAULT ON EMPTY or ON ERROR (MySQL).

functions.name: JSON_OVERLAPS
functions.summary: Returns 1 if two JSON documents share any array element or object key/value pair.

functions.name: JSON_PRETTY
functions.summary: Returns a JSON document formatted for reading, with indentation and one element or member per line.

functions.name: JSON_QUOTE
functions.summary: Wraps a string in double quotes and escapes it so it is a valid JSON string literal.

functions.name: JSON_SCHEMA_VALID
functions.summary: Returns 1 if a JSON document validates against a JSON Schema, else 0.

functions.name: JSON_SCHEMA_VALIDATION_REPORT
functions.summary: Validates a JSON document against a JSON Schema and returns a JSON report explaining any failure. (MySQL only)

functions.name: JSON_STORAGE_SIZE
functions.summary: Returns the number of bytes used to store the binary representation of a JSON document. (MySQL only)

functions.name: JSON_STORAGE_FREE
functions.summary: Returns how many bytes of a JSON column's binary storage were freed by partial in-place updates. (MySQL only)

functions.name: JSON_EXISTS
functions.summary: Returns 1 if a value exists at the given path of a JSON document, else 0. (MariaDB only)

params.name: path
params.doc: A JSON path expression such as '$.a[0]'.

functions.name: JSON_QUERY
functions.summary: Returns the object or array at a path of a JSON document; NULL for a scalar. (MariaDB only)

params.name: path
params.doc: A JSON path expression such as '$.a[0]'.

functions.name: JSON_DETAILED
functions.summary: Returns a JSON document formatted with indentation for reading. (MariaDB only)

functions.name: JSON_COMPACT
functions.summary: Returns a JSON document with all unnecessary spaces removed. (MariaDB only)

functions.name: JSON_LOOSE
functions.summary: Returns a JSON document with spaces added for readability on one line. (MariaDB only)

functions.name: JSON_EQUALS
functions.summary: Returns 1 if two JSON documents are equal regardless of key order and whitespace. (MariaDB only)

functions.name: JSON_NORMALIZE
functions.summary: Returns a JSON document in a canonical form (sorted keys, no extra spaces) for comparing or indexing. (MariaDB only)

functions.name: DATABASE
functions.summary: Returns the name of the default (current) database, or NULL if none is selected.

functions.name: SCHEMA
functions.summary: Returns the name of the default (current) database; a synonym for DATABASE().

functions.name: USER
functions.summary: Returns the user name and host the client connected as, such as 'app@10.0.0.5'.

functions.name: CURRENT_USER
functions.summary: Returns the account (user@host) the server used to authenticate you, which decides your privileges.

functions.name: SESSION_USER
functions.summary: Returns the user name and host the client connected as; a synonym for USER().

functions.name: SYSTEM_USER
functions.summary: Returns the user name and host the client connected as; a synonym for USER().

functions.name: CURRENT_ROLE
functions.summary: Returns the roles active in the current session as a comma-separated list, or NONE.

functions.name: VERSION
functions.summary: Returns the server version string, such as '8.4.2' or '11.4.3-MariaDB'.

functions.name: CONNECTION_ID
functions.summary: Returns the ID of the current connection (thread), as shown in SHOW PROCESSLIST.

functions.name: LAST_INSERT_ID
functions.summary: Returns the first AUTO_INCREMENT value generated by the most recent INSERT on this connection; with an argument, sets it.

params.name: expr
params.doc: A value to return and remember for the next LAST_INSERT_ID() call.

functions.name: ROW_COUNT
functions.summary: Returns the number of rows changed, deleted or inserted by the previous statement; -1 after a SELECT.

functions.name: FOUND_ROWS
functions.summary: Returns the row count a SQL_CALC_FOUND_ROWS query would have had without LIMIT. Deprecated in MySQL; prefer COUNT(*).

functions.name: BENCHMARK
functions.summary: Evaluates an expression count times and returns 0; the elapsed time shown by the client measures its speed.

functions.name: SLEEP
functions.summary: Pauses for the given number of seconds and returns 0, or 1 if interrupted.

params.name: duration
params.doc: Seconds to sleep; may have a fractional part.

functions.name: CHARSET
functions.summary: Returns the character set of a string argument.

functions.name: COLLATION
functions.summary: Returns the collation of a string argument.

functions.name: COERCIBILITY
functions.summary: Returns the collation coercibility of a string, 0 (explicit) to 6 (ignorable); lower values take precedence.

functions.name: ICU_VERSION
functions.summary: Returns the version of the ICU library used for regular expressions. (MySQL only)

functions.name: ROLES_GRAPHML
functions.summary: Returns a GraphML document describing the role graph of the server. (MySQL only)

functions.name: NAME_CONST
functions.summary: Returns the value and gives the result column the given name; used internally by replication.

functions.name: PS_CURRENT_THREAD_ID
functions.summary: Returns the Performance Schema thread ID of the current connection. (MySQL only)

functions.name: PS_THREAD_ID
functions.summary: Returns the Performance Schema thread ID for a connection ID. (MySQL only)

params.name: connection_id
params.doc: A connection ID such as CONNECTION_ID().

functions.name: FORMAT_BYTES
functions.summary: Formats a byte count as a human-readable size with units such as KiB or MiB. (MySQL only)

functions.name: FORMAT_PICO_TIME
functions.summary: Formats a Performance Schema picosecond value as a readable time with units such as ms or s. (MySQL only)

functions.name: SOURCE_POS_WAIT
functions.summary: Waits until a replica has applied changes up to a source binary log position; returns events waited for, or NULL/-1. (MySQL only)

params.name: log_name
params.doc: The source binary log file name.

params.name: timeout
params.doc: Seconds to wait before giving up.

functions.name: MASTER_POS_WAIT
functions.summary: Waits until a replica has applied changes up to a primary binary log position. (MariaDB; removed from MySQL 8.4, use SOURCE_POS_WAIT)

params.name: timeout
params.doc: Seconds to wait before giving up.

functions.name: GTID_SUBSET
functions.summary: Returns 1 if every GTID in the first set is also in the second set. (MySQL only)

functions.name: GTID_SUBTRACT
functions.summary: Returns the GTIDs in the first set that are not in the second. (MySQL only)

functions.name: GET_LOCK
functions.summary: Tries to obtain a named user lock, waiting up to timeout seconds; returns 1 on success, 0 on timeout, NULL on error.

params.name: timeout
params.doc: Seconds to wait; a negative value waits forever.

functions.name: RELEASE_LOCK
functions.summary: Releases a named lock obtained with GET_LOCK; returns 1 if released, 0 if held by another session, NULL if it did not exist.

functions.name: RELEASE_ALL_LOCKS
functions.summary: Releases every named lock held by the current session and returns how many were released.

functions.name: IS_FREE_LOCK
functions.summary: Returns 1 if the named lock is free, 0 if it is in use, NULL on error.

functions.name: IS_USED_LOCK
functions.summary: Returns the connection ID of the session holding the named lock, or NULL if it is free.

functions.name: UUID
functions.summary: Returns a version 1 universally unique identifier as a 36-character string.

functions.name: UUID_SHORT
functions.summary: Returns a 64-bit unique integer, unique while server_id stays unique and the server restarts fewer than 256 times per second.

functions.name: UUID_TO_BIN
functions.summary: Converts a UUID string to a 16-byte binary value; swap_flag 1 moves the time parts first for index-friendly ordering. (MySQL only)

params.name: swap_flag
params.doc: 1 to swap the time-low and time-high parts.

functions.name: BIN_TO_UUID
functions.summary: Converts a 16-byte binary UUID back to its text form; use the same swap_flag used with UUID_TO_BIN. (MySQL only)

params.name: swap_flag
params.doc: 1 if the value was stored with swapped time parts.

functions.name: IS_UUID
functions.summary: Returns 1 if the argument is a valid UUID string, 0 if not. (MySQL only)

functions.name: SYS_GUID
functions.summary: Returns a 32-character hexadecimal globally unique identifier without dashes. (MariaDB only)

functions.name: INET_ATON
functions.summary: Converts an IPv4 address in dotted form to its integer value.

functions.name: INET_NTOA
functions.summary: Converts an integer IPv4 address to dotted-quad text.

functions.name: INET6_ATON
functions.summary: Converts an IPv4 or IPv6 address to its binary form (4 or 16 bytes) in network byte order.

params.name: expr
params.doc: An IPv4 or IPv6 address in text form.

functions.name: INET6_NTOA
functions.summary: Converts a binary IPv4 or IPv6 address to its text form.

functions.name: IS_IPV4
functions.summary: Returns 1 if the string is a valid IPv4 address, else 0.

functions.name: IS_IPV6
functions.summary: Returns 1 if the string is a valid IPv6 address, else 0.

functions.name: IS_IPV4_COMPAT
functions.summary: Returns 1 if a binary IPv6 address is an IPv4-compatible address, else 0.

functions.name: IS_IPV4_MAPPED
functions.summary: Returns 1 if a binary IPv6 address is an IPv4-mapped address, else 0.

functions.name: MD5
functions.summary: Returns the MD5 hash of a string as 32 hexadecimal characters.

functions.name: SHA1
functions.summary: Returns the SHA-1 hash of a string as 40 hexadecimal characters.

functions.name: SHA
functions.summary: Returns the SHA-1 hash of a string; a synonym for SHA1.

functions.name: SHA2
functions.summary: Returns a SHA-2 hash of a string as hexadecimal text; NULL for an unsupported length.

functions.name: AES_ENCRYPT
functions.summary: Encrypts a string with AES using a key; block_encryption_mode picks the mode, and CBC-style modes need an init vector.

params.name: init_vector
params.doc: A 16-byte initialization vector, required by modes such as CBC.

params.name: kdf_options
params.doc: MySQL 8.0.30+: key derivation function name ('hkdf' or 'pbkdf2_hmac') followed by salt and info or iterations.

functions.name: AES_DECRYPT
functions.summary: Decrypts data encrypted with AES_ENCRYPT using the same key, mode and init vector; NULL on bad input.

params.name: init_vector
params.doc: The initialization vector used when encrypting.

params.name: kdf_options
params.doc: MySQL 8.0.30+: the same key derivation options used when encrypting.

functions.name: RANDOM_BYTES
functions.summary: Returns len random bytes from a cryptographically secure generator (MariaDB 10.10+).

functions.name: COMPRESS
functions.summary: Compresses a string with zlib and returns a binary string prefixed with the uncompressed length.

functions.name: UNCOMPRESS
functions.summary: Uncompresses a string compressed with COMPRESS; NULL if it is not valid compressed data.

functions.name: UNCOMPRESSED_LENGTH
functions.summary: Returns the length a COMPRESS-ed string had before compression.

functions.name: VALIDATE_PASSWORD_STRENGTH
functions.summary: Rates a password from 0 (weak) to 100 (strong); needs the validate_password component. (MySQL only)

functions.name: PASSWORD
functions.summary: Returns the native password hash of a string, as stored in the user table. (MariaDB only; removed from MySQL 8.0)

functions.name: STATEMENT_DIGEST
functions.summary: Returns the SHA-256 digest of a statement's normalized form, as used by the Performance Schema. (MySQL only)

functions.name: STATEMENT_DIGEST_TEXT
functions.summary: Returns the normalized digest text of a SQL statement, with literals replaced by ?. (MySQL only)

functions.name: MATCH
functions.summary: Scores rows against a full-text search over FULLTEXT-indexed columns: MATCH (col, …) AGAINST ('words' [IN BOOLEAN MODE]).
functions.example: MATCH (title, body) AGAINST ('+mysql -oracle' IN BOOLEAN MODE)

params.name: column
params.doc: A column of the FULLTEXT index; list all of its columns.

functions.name: NEXTVAL
functions.summary: Returns the next value of a sequence; the same as NEXT VALUE FOR seq. (MariaDB only)

functions.name: LASTVAL
functions.summary: Returns the last value this session got from a sequence; the same as PREVIOUS VALUE FOR seq. (MariaDB only)

functions.name: SETVAL
functions.summary: Sets the next value of a sequence and returns it; NULL if the sequence is already past that value. (MariaDB only)

params.name: is_used
params.doc: If true (the default), the value counts as used and the next one follows it.

params.name: round
params.doc: The cycle round number for cycling sequences.

functions.name: POINT
functions.summary: Constructs a Point from x and y coordinates.

params.name: x
params.doc: The x coordinate (longitude in geographic systems).

functions.name: LINESTRING
functions.summary: Constructs a LineString from Point values.

params.name: pt
params.doc: A Point; at least two are needed.

functions.name: POLYGON
functions.summary: Constructs a Polygon from LineString rings; the first is the outer ring and each must be closed.

functions.name: ST_GEOMFROMTEXT
functions.summary: Constructs a geometry from its Well-Known Text representation.

params.name: srid
params.doc: Spatial reference system ID; the default is 0 (Cartesian).

params.name: options
params.doc: Axis order option, such as 'axis-order=long-lat'. (MySQL only)

functions.name: ST_GEOMFROMWKB
functions.summary: Constructs a geometry from its Well-Known Binary representation.

params.name: srid
params.doc: Spatial reference system ID; the default is 0 (Cartesian).

functions.name: ST_POINTFROMTEXT
functions.summary: Constructs a Point from its Well-Known Text representation.

params.name: srid
params.doc: Spatial reference system ID; the default is 0 (Cartesian).

functions.name: ST_GEOMFROMGEOJSON
functions.summary: Constructs a geometry from a GeoJSON document.

params.name: options
params.doc: How to handle nested dimensions, 1 to 4.

params.name: srid
params.doc: Spatial reference system ID; the default is 4326.

functions.name: ST_ASTEXT
functions.summary: Returns the Well-Known Text representation of a geometry.

functions.name: ST_ASWKB
functions.summary: Returns the Well-Known Binary representation of a geometry.

functions.name: ST_ASGEOJSON
functions.summary: Returns a geometry as a GeoJSON object.

params.name: options
params.doc: Flags for adding a bounding box or CRS member.

functions.name: ST_X
functions.summary: Returns the X coordinate of a Point.

functions.name: ST_Y
functions.summary: Returns the Y coordinate of a Point.

functions.name: ST_LATITUDE
functions.summary: Returns the latitude of a Point in a geographic spatial reference system. (MySQL only)

functions.name: ST_LONGITUDE
functions.summary: Returns the longitude of a Point in a geographic spatial reference system. (MySQL only)

functions.name: ST_SRID
functions.summary: Returns the spatial reference system ID of a geometry; with a second argument returns the geometry with that SRID.

params.name: srid
params.doc: A new SRID to assign. (MySQL only)

functions.name: ST_DISTANCE
functions.summary: Returns the distance between two geometries, in the units of their spatial reference system.

params.name: unit
params.doc: A length unit such as 'metre' or 'foot'. (MySQL only)

functions.name: ST_DISTANCE_SPHERE
functions.summary: Returns the minimum spherical distance in meters between two points (longitude/latitude).

params.name: radius
params.doc: The sphere radius in meters; the default is 6370986.

functions.name: ST_CONTAINS
functions.summary: Returns 1 if g1 completely contains g2, else 0.

functions.name: ST_WITHIN
functions.summary: Returns 1 if g1 lies completely within g2, else 0.

functions.name: ST_INTERSECTS
functions.summary: Returns 1 if g1 and g2 share any point, else 0.

functions.name: ST_DISJOINT
functions.summary: Returns 1 if g1 and g2 share no point, else 0.

functions.name: ST_EQUALS
functions.summary: Returns 1 if g1 and g2 are spatially equal, else 0.

functions.name: ST_TOUCHES
functions.summary: Returns 1 if g1 and g2 touch at their boundaries but their interiors do not intersect.

functions.name: ST_CROSSES
functions.summary: Returns 1 if g1 spatially crosses g2, else 0.

functions.name: ST_OVERLAPS
functions.summary: Returns 1 if g1 and g2 overlap: same dimension, intersecting, and neither contains the other.

functions.name: ST_UNION
functions.summary: Returns a geometry that is the point-set union of two geometries.

functions.name: ST_INTERSECTION
functions.summary: Returns a geometry that is the point-set intersection of two geometries.

functions.name: ST_DIFFERENCE
functions.summary: Returns the part of g1 that does not intersect g2.

functions.name: ST_SYMDIFFERENCE
functions.summary: Returns the parts of g1 and g2 that do not intersect each other.

functions.name: ST_AREA
functions.summary: Returns the area of a Polygon or MultiPolygon.

functions.name: ST_LENGTH
functions.summary: Returns the length of a LineString or MultiLineString.

params.name: unit
params.doc: A length unit such as 'metre'. (MySQL only)

functions.name: ST_BUFFER
functions.summary: Returns a geometry covering all points within a distance of the given geometry.

functions.name: ST_CENTROID
functions.summary: Returns the mathematical centroid of a geometry as a Point.

functions.name: ST_ENVELOPE
functions.summary: Returns the minimum bounding rectangle of a geometry.

functions.name: ST_CONVEXHULL
functions.summary: Returns the convex hull of a geometry.

functions.name: ST_ISVALID
functions.summary: Returns 1 if a geometry is valid according to OGC rules, else 0.

functions.name: ST_ISEMPTY
functions.summary: Returns 1 if a geometry is empty, else 0.

functions.name: ST_ISSIMPLE
functions.summary: Returns 1 if a geometry has no anomalous points such as self-intersections, else 0.

functions.name: ST_ISCLOSED
functions.summary: Returns 1 if a LineString's start and end points are the same, else 0.

functions.name: ST_GEOMETRYTYPE
functions.summary: Returns the name of a geometry's type, such as 'POINT' or 'POLYGON'.

functions.name: ST_DIMENSION
functions.summary: Returns the inherent dimension of a geometry: 0 for points, 1 for lines, 2 for polygons.

functions.name: ST_NUMPOINTS
functions.summary: Returns the number of Points in a LineString.

functions.name: ST_STARTPOINT
functions.summary: Returns the first Point of a LineString.

functions.name: ST_ENDPOINT
functions.summary: Returns the last Point of a LineString.

functions.name: ST_EXTERIORRING
functions.summary: Returns the exterior ring of a Polygon as a LineString.

functions.name: ST_NUMGEOMETRIES
functions.summary: Returns the number of geometries in a GeometryCollection or multi-geometry.

functions.name: ST_ASBINARY
functions.summary: Returns the Well-Known Binary representation of a geometry; a synonym for ST_ASWKB.

functions.name: ST_POINTN
functions.summary: Returns the N-th Point of a LineString (1-based).

functions.name: ST_GEOMETRYN
functions.summary: Returns the N-th geometry of a GeometryCollection or multi-geometry (1-based).

functions.name: ST_TRANSFORM
functions.summary: Transforms a geometry from its spatial reference system to another. (MySQL only)

functions.name: ST_MAKEENVELOPE
functions.summary: Returns the rectangle formed by two corner Points. (MySQL only)

functions.name: MBRCONTAINS
functions.summary: Returns 1 if the minimum bounding rectangle of g1 contains that of g2.

functions.name: MBRINTERSECTS
functions.summary: Returns 1 if the minimum bounding rectangles of g1 and g2 intersect.

functions.name: STRING_TO_VECTOR
functions.summary: Converts a text list of floats such as '[1.5, 2, 3]' to a VECTOR value. (MySQL 9.0+)

params.name: str
params.doc: The vector as text in square brackets.

functions.name: TO_VECTOR
functions.summary: Converts a text list of floats to a VECTOR value; a synonym for STRING_TO_VECTOR. (MySQL 9.0+)

params.name: str
params.doc: The vector as text in square brackets.

functions.name: VECTOR_TO_STRING
functions.summary: Returns the text form of a VECTOR value, such as '[1.00000e+00,2.00000e+00]'. (MySQL 9.0+)

functions.name: FROM_VECTOR
functions.summary: Returns the text form of a VECTOR value; a synonym for VECTOR_TO_STRING. (MySQL 9.0+)

functions.name: VECTOR_DIM
functions.summary: Returns the number of dimensions of a VECTOR value. (MySQL 9.0+)

functions.name: VEC_FROMTEXT
functions.summary: Converts a JSON array of numbers to a VECTOR value. (MariaDB 11.7+)

params.name: text
params.doc: The vector as a JSON array such as '[0.1, 0.2]'.

functions.name: VEC_TOTEXT
functions.summary: Returns a VECTOR value as a JSON array of numbers. (MariaDB 11.7+)

functions.name: VEC_DISTANCE_EUCLIDEAN
functions.summary: Returns the Euclidean (L2) distance between two vectors. (MariaDB 11.7+)

functions.name: VEC_DISTANCE_COSINE
functions.summary: Returns the cosine distance between two vectors. (MariaDB 11.7+)

functions.name: VEC_DISTANCE
functions.summary: Returns the distance between two vectors using the metric of the vector index on the column. (MariaDB 11.7+)

keywords.name: LIMIT
keywords.doc: Restricts how many rows a query returns, optionally after skipping some rows.
keywords.syntax: LIMIT row_count [OFFSET offset] | LIMIT offset, row_count

keywords.name: OFFSET
keywords.doc: Skips the given number of rows before LIMIT starts counting.

keywords.name: IF
keywords.doc: Guards DDL so it does nothing when the object already exists or is missing; also the IF … THEN … END IF statement in stored programs.

keywords.name: IF EXISTS
keywords.doc: Makes DROP or ALTER succeed silently (with a note) when the object does not exist.

keywords.name: IF NOT EXISTS
keywords.doc: Makes CREATE succeed silently (with a note) when the object already exists.
keywords.syntax: CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS t (…)

keywords.name: ELSEIF
keywords.doc: Adds another condition branch to an IF statement in a stored program.
keywords.syntax: IF c1 THEN … ELSEIF c2 THEN … END IF

keywords.name: SHOW
keywords.doc: Displays server metadata: databases, tables, columns, indexes, status, variables, grants, processes and more.

keywords.name: DESCRIBE
keywords.doc: Shows the columns of a table (like SHOW COLUMNS), or the execution plan of a statement (like EXPLAIN).

keywords.name: EXPLAIN
keywords.doc: Shows the execution plan for a statement; EXPLAIN ANALYZE runs it and reports actual timings (MySQL), ANALYZE statement in MariaDB.

keywords.name: USE
keywords.doc: Selects the default database for the session.

keywords.name: DATABASE
keywords.doc: A database (a schema in MySQL terms), as in CREATE DATABASE or DROP DATABASE.
keywords.syntax: CREATE DATABASE [IF NOT EXISTS] db_name [CHARACTER SET cs] [COLLATE coll]

keywords.name: SCHEMA
keywords.doc: A synonym for DATABASE in DDL statements.

keywords.name: DATABASES
keywords.doc: Used in SHOW DATABASES to list the databases you can see.

keywords.name: TABLES
keywords.doc: Used in SHOW TABLES, LOCK TABLES and FLUSH TABLES.

keywords.name: COLUMNS
keywords.doc: Used in SHOW COLUMNS to list a table's columns, and in LOAD DATA as a synonym for FIELDS.

keywords.name: INDEXES
keywords.doc: Used in SHOW INDEXES to list a table's indexes.

keywords.name: STATUS
keywords.doc: Used in SHOW STATUS and SHOW TABLE STATUS to report server or table statistics.

keywords.name: VARIABLES
keywords.doc: Used in SHOW VARIABLES to list system variable values.

keywords.name: PROCESSLIST
keywords.doc: Used in SHOW PROCESSLIST to list the running connections and their statements.

keywords.name: GRANTS
keywords.doc: Used in SHOW GRANTS to list an account's privileges.

keywords.name: WARNINGS
keywords.doc: Used in SHOW WARNINGS to list the notes, warnings and errors of the last statement.

keywords.name: ERRORS
keywords.doc: Used in SHOW ERRORS to list the errors of the last statement.

keywords.name: ENGINES
keywords.doc: Used in SHOW ENGINES to list the available storage engines.

keywords.name: PROCEDURE
keywords.doc: A stored procedure, created with CREATE PROCEDURE and run with CALL.
keywords.syntax: CREATE PROCEDURE name ([IN | OUT | INOUT] param type, …) BEGIN … END

keywords.name: FUNCTION
keywords.doc: A stored function, created with CREATE FUNCTION and called in expressions.
keywords.syntax: CREATE FUNCTION name (param type, …) RETURNS type [DETERMINISTIC] BEGIN … RETURN expr; END

keywords.name: RETURNS
keywords.doc: Declares the return type of a stored function.

keywords.name: RETURN
keywords.doc: Ends a stored function and returns a value.

keywords.name: DETERMINISTIC
keywords.doc: Declares that a stored routine always gives the same result for the same arguments; NOT DETERMINISTIC is the default.
keywords.syntax: CREATE FUNCTION f (…) RETURNS INT DETERMINISTIC …

keywords.name: OUT
keywords.doc: Marks a stored procedure parameter as output only.

keywords.name: INOUT
keywords.doc: Marks a stored procedure parameter as both input and output.

keywords.name: READS SQL DATA
keywords.doc: Declares that a routine reads data but does not modify it.

keywords.name: MODIFIES SQL DATA
keywords.doc: Declares that a routine may modify data.

keywords.name: CONTAINS SQL
keywords.doc: Declares that a routine contains SQL but does not read or write table data (the default).

keywords.name: NO SQL
keywords.doc: Declares that a routine contains no SQL statements.

keywords.name: CALL
keywords.doc: Invokes a stored procedure.

keywords.name: DECLARE
keywords.doc: Declares a local variable, condition, cursor or handler at the start of a BEGIN … END block.

keywords.name: DELIMITER
keywords.doc: A client command (mysql and most tools) that changes the statement terminator so routine bodies can contain semicolons.

keywords.name: DO
keywords.doc: Evaluates expressions without returning results; also starts an event body (ON SCHEDULE … DO) and a WHILE loop body.

keywords.name: LOOP
keywords.doc: Repeats a block of statements until LEAVE exits it.

keywords.name: REPEAT
keywords.doc: Repeats a block of statements until a condition becomes true; the body runs at least once.

keywords.name: UNTIL
keywords.doc: Gives the exit condition of a REPEAT loop.

keywords.name: WHILE
keywords.doc: Repeats a block of statements while a condition is true.

keywords.name: LEAVE
keywords.doc: Exits a labeled loop or BEGIN … END block.

keywords.name: ITERATE
keywords.doc: Starts the next iteration of a labeled loop.

keywords.name: HANDLER
keywords.doc: Declares what to do when a condition occurs in a stored program; also the HANDLER statement for direct index access.
keywords.syntax: DECLARE {CONTINUE | EXIT} HANDLER FOR condition statement

keywords.name: CONTINUE
keywords.doc: A handler type: after the handler runs, execution continues after the failing statement.
keywords.syntax: DECLARE CONTINUE HANDLER FOR NOT FOUND SET done = 1

keywords.name: EXIT
keywords.doc: A handler type: after the handler runs, the enclosing BEGIN … END block ends.

keywords.name: CONDITION
keywords.doc: Declares a named error condition in a stored program.

keywords.name: SQLSTATE
keywords.doc: Names a five-character SQLSTATE code in a handler, condition or SIGNAL.

keywords.name: SQLEXCEPTION
keywords.doc: In a handler, matches every SQLSTATE that is not a warning, not found or success.

keywords.name: SQLWARNING
keywords.doc: In a handler, matches every SQLSTATE that starts with '01'.

keywords.name: NOT FOUND
keywords.doc: In a handler, matches SQLSTATE '02000', raised when a cursor runs out of rows.
keywords.syntax: DECLARE CONTINUE HANDLER FOR NOT FOUND SET done = 1

keywords.name: SIGNAL
keywords.doc: Raises an error or warning from a stored program.

keywords.name: RESIGNAL
keywords.doc: Re-raises the condition being handled, optionally changing its information.

keywords.name: GET DIAGNOSTICS
keywords.doc: Reads information about the last statement's conditions into variables.

keywords.name: CURSOR
keywords.doc: Declares a cursor over a SELECT in a stored program.

keywords.name: OPEN
keywords.doc: Opens a declared cursor.

keywords.name: FETCH
keywords.doc: Reads the next row of an open cursor into variables.
keywords.syntax: FETCH [NEXT FROM] cursor_name INTO var [, var …]

keywords.name: CLOSE
keywords.doc: Closes an open cursor.

keywords.name: PREPARE
keywords.doc: Prepares a statement from a string for later execution with EXECUTE.

keywords.name: EXECUTE
keywords.doc: Runs a prepared statement, binding user variables to its ? placeholders.

keywords.name: EXECUTE IMMEDIATE
keywords.doc: Prepares, runs and frees a statement given as a string expression in one step. (MariaDB only)

keywords.name: DEALLOCATE PREPARE
keywords.doc: Frees a prepared statement.

keywords.name: AUTO_INCREMENT
keywords.doc: Makes an integer column generate the next number automatically on insert; also the table option for its next value.

keywords.name: ENGINE
keywords.doc: Sets the storage engine of a table, such as InnoDB, MyISAM, MEMORY or Aria (MariaDB).

keywords.name: CHARACTER SET
keywords.doc: Sets the character set of a database, table, column or string, such as utf8mb4.

keywords.name: CHARSET
keywords.doc: A synonym for CHARACTER SET in table and column definitions.

keywords.name: ROW_FORMAT
keywords.doc: Sets how InnoDB stores a table's rows: DYNAMIC, COMPRESSED, COMPACT or REDUNDANT.

keywords.name: COMMENT
keywords.doc: Attaches a descriptive comment to a table, column, index or routine.

keywords.name: UNSIGNED
keywords.doc: Makes a numeric column hold only non-negative values, doubling the positive range for integers; also a CAST target.

keywords.name: SIGNED
keywords.doc: The default signed integer attribute; as a CAST target converts to a signed BIGINT.

keywords.name: ZEROFILL
keywords.doc: Pads a numeric column's displayed value with leading zeros; deprecated in MySQL 8.

keywords.name: ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE
keywords.doc: Turns an INSERT into an update of the existing row when it would violate a PRIMARY KEY or UNIQUE index.
keywords.syntax: INSERT INTO t (id, n) VALUES (1, 1) ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE n = n + 1

keywords.name: DUPLICATE
keywords.doc: Part of INSERT … ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE.

keywords.name: REPLACE INTO
keywords.doc: Inserts a row, first deleting any existing row with the same PRIMARY KEY or UNIQUE value.

keywords.name: IGNORE
keywords.doc: Turns errors such as duplicate keys into warnings and skips the offending rows in INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE and LOAD DATA.

keywords.name: STRAIGHT_JOIN
keywords.doc: Forces tables to be joined in the order they are listed in the FROM clause.
keywords.syntax: SELECT … FROM a STRAIGHT_JOIN b ON …

keywords.name: SQL_CALC_FOUND_ROWS
keywords.doc: Makes FOUND_ROWS() return the row count the query would have had without LIMIT. Deprecated in MySQL.

keywords.name: SQL_NO_CACHE
keywords.doc: Asks the server not to cache the result; a no-op in MySQL 8 (no query cache), still honored by MariaDB's query cache.

keywords.name: SQL_BUFFER_RESULT
keywords.doc: Forces the result into a temporary table so table locks are released early.

keywords.name: SQL_SMALL_RESULT
keywords.doc: Hints that a GROUP BY or DISTINCT result is small, so an in-memory temporary table is used.

keywords.name: SQL_BIG_RESULT
keywords.doc: Hints that a GROUP BY or DISTINCT result is large, so an on-disk temporary table or sorting is used.

keywords.name: HIGH_PRIORITY
keywords.doc: Gives a SELECT or INSERT priority over pending writes on table-locking engines such as MyISAM.

keywords.name: LOW_PRIORITY
keywords.doc: Delays an INSERT, UPDATE or DELETE until no clients are reading the table (table-locking engines only).

keywords.name: DELAYED
keywords.doc: Legacy INSERT DELAYED; accepted but treated as a normal INSERT in current versions.

keywords.name: QUICK
keywords.doc: Speeds up DELETE on MyISAM tables by not merging index leaves.

keywords.name: FORCE INDEX
keywords.doc: Tells the optimizer to use one of the listed indexes, treating a table scan as very expensive.
keywords.syntax: SELECT … FROM t FORCE INDEX (idx_name) WHERE …

keywords.name: USE INDEX
keywords.doc: Tells the optimizer to consider only the listed indexes.
keywords.syntax: SELECT … FROM t USE INDEX (idx_a, idx_b)

keywords.name: IGNORE INDEX
keywords.doc: Tells the optimizer not to use the listed indexes.

keywords.name: FOR UPDATE
keywords.doc: Locks the rows a SELECT reads so other transactions cannot change them until you commit.

keywords.name: FOR SHARE
keywords.doc: Takes shared locks on the rows a SELECT reads (MySQL 8); LOCK IN SHARE MODE is the older form.

keywords.name: LOCK IN SHARE MODE
keywords.doc: Takes shared locks on the rows a SELECT reads.

keywords.name: NOWAIT
keywords.doc: Makes a locking read fail immediately instead of waiting for a locked row.

keywords.name: SKIP LOCKED
keywords.doc: Makes a locking read skip rows that other transactions have locked.

keywords.name: WITH ROLLUP
keywords.doc: Adds super-aggregate rows (subtotals and a grand total) to GROUP BY results.
keywords.syntax: GROUP BY year, region WITH ROLLUP

keywords.name: REGEXP
keywords.doc: Tests whether a string matches a regular expression; NOT REGEXP negates.

keywords.name: RLIKE
keywords.doc: A synonym for REGEXP.

keywords.name: SOUNDS LIKE
keywords.doc: Tests whether two strings sound alike; the same as SOUNDEX(a) = SOUNDEX(b).

keywords.name: DIV
keywords.doc: Integer division: divides and discards the fractional part.

keywords.name: MOD
keywords.doc: The modulo operator; the same as % and MOD(N, M).

keywords.name: XOR
keywords.doc: Logical exclusive OR: true when exactly one operand is true.

keywords.name: INTERVAL
keywords.doc: Introduces a time interval in date arithmetic and event schedules.

keywords.name: MEMBER OF
keywords.doc: Tests whether a value is an element of a JSON array. (MySQL only)

keywords.name: TRUNCATE
keywords.doc: Removes all rows from a table quickly by recreating it and resets AUTO_INCREMENT.

keywords.name: RENAME
keywords.doc: Renames tables, columns, indexes or users.

keywords.name: MODIFY
keywords.doc: In ALTER TABLE, changes a column's definition without renaming it.
keywords.syntax: ALTER TABLE t MODIFY [COLUMN] col new_definition

keywords.name: CHANGE
keywords.doc: In ALTER TABLE, renames a column and/or changes its definition.
keywords.syntax: ALTER TABLE t CHANGE [COLUMN] old_name new_name definition

keywords.name: AFTER
keywords.doc: Places a new or modified column after another column; also a trigger timing.
keywords.syntax: ALTER TABLE t ADD COLUMN c INT AFTER b

keywords.name: FIRST
keywords.doc: Places a new or modified column first in the table.
keywords.syntax: ALTER TABLE t ADD COLUMN c INT FIRST

keywords.name: BEFORE
keywords.doc: A trigger timing: the trigger runs before the row change.
keywords.syntax: CREATE TRIGGER trg BEFORE INSERT ON t FOR EACH ROW …

keywords.name: FOR EACH ROW
keywords.doc: Makes a trigger run once for every affected row (the only kind MySQL supports).

keywords.name: TEMPORARY
keywords.doc: Creates a table visible only to the current session and dropped when it ends.

keywords.name: RECURSIVE
keywords.doc: Lets a common table expression refer to itself.
keywords.syntax: WITH RECURSIVE cte AS (… UNION ALL … FROM cte) SELECT …

keywords.name: LATERAL
keywords.doc: Lets a derived table refer to columns of tables earlier in the same FROM clause. (MySQL 8.0.14+)
keywords.syntax: FROM t, LATERAL (SELECT … WHERE x = t.x) AS d

keywords.name: WINDOW
keywords.doc: Defines a named window that OVER clauses can refer to.
keywords.syntax: WINDOW w AS (PARTITION BY a ORDER BY b)

keywords.name: GRANT
keywords.doc: Gives privileges or roles to an account.
keywords.syntax: GRANT SELECT, INSERT ON db.* TO 'user'@'host'

keywords.name: REVOKE
keywords.doc: Removes privileges or roles from an account.

keywords.name: PRIVILEGES
keywords.doc: Used in GRANT ALL PRIVILEGES and FLUSH PRIVILEGES.
keywords.syntax: GRANT ALL PRIVILEGES ON db.* TO 'user'@'host'

keywords.name: USER
keywords.doc: An account, as in CREATE USER, ALTER USER and DROP USER.

keywords.name: ROLE
keywords.doc: A named collection of privileges that can be granted to accounts.

keywords.name: IDENTIFIED BY
keywords.doc: Sets an account's password.

keywords.name: IDENTIFIED WITH
keywords.doc: Sets an account's authentication plugin (MySQL) or plugin/method (MariaDB).
keywords.syntax: CREATE USER 'u'@'%' IDENTIFIED WITH caching_sha2_password BY 'password'

keywords.name: LOCK TABLES
keywords.doc: Takes explicit READ or WRITE locks on tables for the current session.
keywords.syntax: LOCK TABLES t1 READ, t2 WRITE

keywords.name: UNLOCK TABLES
keywords.doc: Releases the table locks held by the current session.

keywords.name: START TRANSACTION
keywords.doc: Begins a transaction, optionally with a consistent snapshot or read-only.
keywords.syntax: START TRANSACTION [WITH CONSISTENT SNAPSHOT | READ ONLY | READ WRITE]

keywords.name: WORK
keywords.doc: Optional word in BEGIN WORK, COMMIT WORK and ROLLBACK WORK.

keywords.name: ISOLATION LEVEL
keywords.doc: Sets the transaction isolation level.
keywords.syntax: SET [GLOBAL | SESSION] TRANSACTION ISOLATION LEVEL {READ UNCOMMITTED | READ COMMITTED | REPEATABLE READ | SERIALIZABLE}

keywords.name: READ UNCOMMITTED
keywords.doc: Isolation level that lets a transaction see other transactions' uncommitted changes (dirty reads).

keywords.name: READ COMMITTED
keywords.doc: Isolation level where each statement sees only data committed before it began.

keywords.name: REPEATABLE READ
keywords.doc: InnoDB's default isolation level: every read in a transaction sees the same snapshot.

keywords.name: SERIALIZABLE
keywords.doc: The strictest isolation level: plain SELECTs take shared locks as if they were FOR SHARE.

keywords.name: STORED
keywords.doc: A generated column whose value is computed on write and stored in the row.

keywords.name: VIRTUAL
keywords.doc: A generated column computed when read and not stored (the default).

keywords.name: GENERATED
keywords.doc: Part of GENERATED ALWAYS AS, which defines a generated column.
keywords.syntax: col INT GENERATED ALWAYS AS (a * b) STORED

keywords.name: ALWAYS
keywords.doc: Part of GENERATED ALWAYS AS.

keywords.name: INVISIBLE
keywords.doc: Hides a column from SELECT * or an index from the optimizer while keeping it.
keywords.syntax: ALTER TABLE t ALTER INDEX idx INVISIBLE

keywords.name: VISIBLE
keywords.doc: Makes an invisible index or column visible again.
keywords.syntax: ALTER TABLE t ALTER INDEX idx VISIBLE

keywords.name: FULLTEXT
keywords.doc: An index type for full-text search with MATCH … AGAINST.
keywords.syntax: CREATE FULLTEXT INDEX ft ON t (title, body)

keywords.name: SPATIAL
keywords.doc: An R-tree index type for geometry columns.
keywords.syntax: CREATE SPATIAL INDEX sp ON t (location)

keywords.name: AGAINST
keywords.doc: Gives the search string of a full-text MATCH.

keywords.name: IN BOOLEAN MODE
keywords.doc: Full-text search mode that honors operators such as +, -, * and quotes.

keywords.name: IN NATURAL LANGUAGE MODE
keywords.doc: The default full-text search mode, ranking rows by relevance to the phrase.

keywords.name: WITH QUERY EXPANSION
keywords.doc: Full-text search that runs a second search with words from the best first-round matches.

keywords.name: CASCADE
keywords.doc: A foreign key action that deletes or updates child rows along with the parent row.
keywords.syntax: FOREIGN KEY (a) REFERENCES p (id) ON DELETE CASCADE

keywords.name: RESTRICT
keywords.doc: A foreign key action that rejects deleting or updating a parent row that has children.

keywords.name: NO ACTION
keywords.doc: A foreign key action; in InnoDB the same as RESTRICT.

keywords.name: ON DELETE
keywords.doc: Sets what happens to child rows when a referenced parent row is deleted.
keywords.syntax: ON DELETE {CASCADE | SET NULL | RESTRICT | NO ACTION}

keywords.name: ON UPDATE
keywords.doc: Sets what happens to child rows when a parent key changes; for TIMESTAMP/DATETIME columns, sets the value on every update.
keywords.syntax: updated_at TIMESTAMP DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP ON UPDATE CURRENT_TIMESTAMP

keywords.name: EVENT
keywords.doc: A scheduled task run by the event scheduler.
keywords.syntax: CREATE EVENT name ON SCHEDULE EVERY 1 DAY DO statement

keywords.name: ON SCHEDULE
keywords.doc: Sets when an event runs.
keywords.syntax: ON SCHEDULE {AT timestamp | EVERY interval [STARTS ts] [ENDS ts]}

keywords.name: SCHEDULE
keywords.doc: Part of ON SCHEDULE in CREATE EVENT.

keywords.name: EVERY
keywords.doc: Makes an event recur at a fixed interval.

keywords.name: STARTS
keywords.doc: Sets when a recurring event first runs.

keywords.name: ENDS
keywords.doc: Sets when a recurring event stops running.

keywords.name: ALGORITHM
keywords.doc: Chooses how a view is processed (MERGE, TEMPTABLE, UNDEFINED) or how ALTER TABLE works (INSTANT, INPLACE, COPY).
keywords.syntax: ALTER TABLE t ADD COLUMN c INT, ALGORITHM = INSTANT

keywords.name: LOCK
keywords.doc: In ALTER TABLE, sets how much concurrent access is allowed: NONE, SHARED, EXCLUSIVE or DEFAULT.
keywords.syntax: ALTER TABLE t ADD INDEX i (c), LOCK = NONE

keywords.name: DEFINER
keywords.doc: The account whose privileges a view, routine, trigger or event runs with under SQL SECURITY DEFINER.

keywords.name: SQL SECURITY
keywords.doc: Chooses whether a view or routine runs with the definer's or the invoker's privileges.

keywords.name: INVOKER
keywords.doc: Runs a view or routine with the privileges of the user who calls it.

keywords.name: LOAD DATA
keywords.doc: Bulk-loads rows from a text file into a table.
keywords.syntax: LOAD DATA [LOCAL] INFILE 'file' INTO TABLE t FIELDS TERMINATED BY ',' LINES TERMINATED BY '\n' IGNORE 1 LINES

keywords.name: LOCAL
keywords.doc: Reads a LOAD DATA file from the client host instead of the server.

keywords.name: INFILE
keywords.doc: Names the file LOAD DATA reads.
keywords.syntax: LOAD DATA INFILE 'file_name' INTO TABLE t

keywords.name: OUTFILE
keywords.doc: Writes a SELECT result to a file on the server host.
keywords.syntax: SELECT … INTO OUTFILE '/tmp/out.csv' FIELDS TERMINATED BY ','

keywords.name: DUMPFILE
keywords.doc: Writes a single SELECT row to a file without any formatting.
keywords.syntax: SELECT blob_col INTO DUMPFILE '/tmp/x.bin' FROM t

keywords.name: FIELDS
keywords.doc: Starts the field format options of LOAD DATA or SELECT … INTO OUTFILE.
keywords.syntax: FIELDS TERMINATED BY ',' OPTIONALLY ENCLOSED BY '"' ESCAPED BY '\\'

keywords.name: TERMINATED
keywords.doc: Sets the field or line separator: TERMINATED BY 'string'.

keywords.name: ENCLOSED
keywords.doc: Sets the quote character around fields: [OPTIONALLY] ENCLOSED BY 'char'.

keywords.name: OPTIONALLY
keywords.doc: Quotes only string fields when combined with ENCLOSED BY.

keywords.name: ESCAPED
keywords.doc: Sets the escape character for fields: ESCAPED BY 'char'.

keywords.name: LINES
keywords.doc: Starts the line format options of LOAD DATA or SELECT … INTO OUTFILE; also IGNORE n LINES.

keywords.name: STARTING
keywords.doc: Sets a prefix that each line must start with: STARTING BY 'string'.

keywords.name: KILL
keywords.doc: Ends a connection, or with QUERY only its running statement.

keywords.name: FLUSH
keywords.doc: Clears or reloads internal caches, logs, privileges or tables.

keywords.name: OPTIMIZE
