keywords.doc: Reorganizes a table's storage and rebuilds its indexes to reclaim space.

keywords.name: ANALYZE
keywords.doc: Updates a table's index statistics or histograms; in MariaDB, ANALYZE statement also runs it and reports actual row counts.
keywords.syntax: ANALYZE TABLE tbl_name [UPDATE HISTOGRAM ON col]

keywords.name: REPAIR
keywords.doc: Repairs a possibly corrupted MyISAM, ARCHIVE, CSV or Aria table.

keywords.name: GLOBAL
keywords.doc: Sets or shows a system variable's server-wide value.

keywords.name: SESSION
keywords.doc: Sets or shows a system variable's value for the current connection only (the default).

keywords.name: PERSIST
keywords.doc: Sets a global system variable and saves it so it survives restarts. (MySQL only)

keywords.name: PERSIST_ONLY
keywords.doc: Saves a system variable setting for the next restart without changing the running value. (MySQL only)

keywords.name: DUAL
keywords.doc: A dummy table name for SELECTs that need no table.

keywords.name: SEPARATOR
keywords.doc: Sets the string placed between values in GROUP_CONCAT.

keywords.name: RETURNING
keywords.doc: Returns columns of the rows affected by INSERT, REPLACE or DELETE. (MariaDB only)
keywords.syntax: DELETE FROM t WHERE id = 1 RETURNING id, name

keywords.name: SEQUENCE
keywords.doc: A sequence object that generates numbers. (MariaDB only)
keywords.syntax: CREATE SEQUENCE s START WITH 1 INCREMENT BY 1

keywords.name: NEXT VALUE FOR
keywords.doc: Returns the next value of a sequence. (MariaDB only)

keywords.name: WITH SYSTEM VERSIONING
keywords.doc: Makes a table system-versioned so its row history can be queried. (MariaDB only)
keywords.syntax: CREATE TABLE t (…) WITH SYSTEM VERSIONING

keywords.name: FOR SYSTEM_TIME
keywords.doc: Queries a system-versioned table as of a point or range in time. (MariaDB only)
keywords.syntax: SELECT … FROM t FOR SYSTEM_TIME AS OF TIMESTAMP '2024-01-01 00:00:00'

constants.name: TRUE
constants.doc: The boolean true value; in MySQL it is simply the integer 1.

constants.name: FALSE
constants.doc: The boolean false value; in MySQL it is simply the integer 0.

constants.name: UNKNOWN
constants.doc: The third boolean truth value, used in IS [NOT] UNKNOWN; the same as NULL for a boolean expression.

types.name: TINYINT
types.doc: 1-byte integer: -128 to 127, or 0 to 255 UNSIGNED. TINYINT(1) is the conventional boolean.

types.name: SMALLINT
types.doc: 2-byte integer: -32768 to 32767, or 0 to 65535 UNSIGNED.

types.name: MEDIUMINT
types.doc: 3-byte integer: -8388608 to 8388607, or 0 to 16777215 UNSIGNED.

types.name: INT
types.doc: 4-byte integer: -2147483648 to 2147483647, or 0 to 4294967295 UNSIGNED. The display width INT(n) is deprecated.

types.name: INTEGER
types.doc: A synonym for INT: a 4-byte integer.

types.name: BIGINT
types.doc: 8-byte integer: -2^63 to 2^63-1, or 0 to 2^64-1 UNSIGNED.

types.name: DECIMAL
types.doc: Exact fixed-point number with up to 65 digits (M) and 30 after the point (D); the default is DECIMAL(10,0).

types.name: DEC
types.doc: A synonym for DECIMAL.

types.name: NUMERIC
types.doc: A synonym for DECIMAL.

types.name: FIXED
types.doc: A synonym for DECIMAL.

types.name: FLOAT
types.doc: 4-byte single-precision approximate number; FLOAT(p) with p over 24 gives a DOUBLE.

types.name: DOUBLE
types.doc: 8-byte double-precision approximate number; DOUBLE PRECISION is a synonym.

types.name: REAL
types.doc: A synonym for DOUBLE, or for FLOAT when sql_mode includes REAL_AS_FLOAT.

types.name: BIT
types.doc: A bit-field of 1 to 64 bits, written with b'0101' literals.

types.name: BOOL
types.doc: A synonym for TINYINT(1); 0 is false and any non-zero value is true.

types.name: BOOLEAN
types.doc: A synonym for TINYINT(1); 0 is false and any non-zero value is true.

types.name: SERIAL
types.doc: Shorthand for BIGINT UNSIGNED NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT UNIQUE.

types.name: DATE
types.doc: A calendar date from '1000-01-01' to '9999-12-31', shown as 'YYYY-MM-DD'.

types.name: DATETIME
types.doc: A date and time from '1000-01-01 00:00:00' to '9999-12-31 23:59:59', with optional fractional seconds; no time zone conversion.

types.name: TIMESTAMP
types.doc: A UTC-stored date and time from 1970-01-01 to 2038-01-19 (later in MariaDB 11.5+ on 64-bit), converted to and from the session time zone.

types.name: TIME
types.doc: A time of day or elapsed time from '-838:59:59' to '838:59:59', with optional fractional seconds.

types.name: YEAR
types.doc: A 4-digit year from 1901 to 2155, or 0000.

types.name: CHAR
types.doc: Fixed-length string of 0 to 255 characters, padded with spaces on storage; CHARACTER is a synonym.

types.name: VARCHAR
types.doc: Variable-length string up to M characters; the whole row is limited to 65,535 bytes.

types.name: NCHAR
types.doc: Fixed-length string in the national character set (utf8mb3); NATIONAL CHAR is a synonym.

types.name: NVARCHAR
types.doc: Variable-length string in the national character set (utf8mb3); NATIONAL VARCHAR is a synonym.

types.name: BINARY
types.doc: Fixed-length byte string of 0 to 255 bytes, padded with 0x00. As an operator (BINARY expr) it casts to a binary string, deprecated in MySQL 8.

types.name: VARBINARY
types.doc: Variable-length byte string up to M bytes.

types.name: TINYBLOB
types.doc: Binary large object up to 255 bytes.

types.name: BLOB
types.doc: Binary large object up to 65,535 bytes (64 KB); BLOB(M) picks the smallest BLOB type that fits M bytes.

types.name: MEDIUMBLOB
types.doc: Binary large object up to 16 MB.

types.name: LONGBLOB
types.doc: Binary large object up to 4 GB.

types.name: TINYTEXT
types.doc: Text up to 255 bytes.

types.name: TEXT
types.doc: Text up to 65,535 bytes (64 KB); TEXT(M) picks the smallest TEXT type that fits M characters.

types.name: MEDIUMTEXT
types.doc: Text up to 16 MB.

types.name: LONGTEXT
types.doc: Text up to 4 GB.

types.name: ENUM
types.doc: A string that must be one of a fixed list of values (up to 65,535), stored as an index number.

types.name: JSON
types.doc: A validated JSON document; MySQL stores it in an optimized binary format, MariaDB as LONGTEXT with a JSON_VALID check.

types.name: GEOMETRY
types.doc: A spatial value of any geometry type.

types.name: POINT
types.doc: A spatial value holding a single X/Y coordinate.

types.name: LINESTRING
types.doc: A spatial value holding a line of connected points.

types.name: POLYGON
types.doc: A spatial value holding a polygon with an outer ring and optional holes.

types.name: MULTIPOINT
types.doc: A spatial collection of Points.

types.name: MULTILINESTRING
types.doc: A spatial collection of LineStrings.

types.name: MULTIPOLYGON
types.doc: A spatial collection of Polygons.

types.name: GEOMETRYCOLLECTION
types.doc: A spatial collection of geometries of any type; GEOMCOLLECTION is a MySQL synonym.

types.name: VECTOR
types.doc: A fixed-dimension array of 4-byte floats for embeddings. (MySQL 9.0+, MariaDB 11.7+)

types.name: UUID
types.doc: A 128-bit UUID stored in 16 bytes and shown in standard text form. (MariaDB only)

types.name: INET4
types.doc: An IPv4 address stored in 4 bytes. (MariaDB only)

types.name: INET6
types.doc: An IPv6 (or IPv4-mapped) address stored in 16 bytes. (MariaDB only)

variables.name: @@autocommit
variables.doc: Whether each statement commits on its own (1) or waits for an explicit COMMIT (0). Set per session.

variables.name: @@sql_mode
variables.doc: The SQL modes in effect, such as STRICT_TRANS_TABLES, ANSI_QUOTES and NO_BACKSLASH_ESCAPES; they change how the server parses and validates statements.

variables.name: @@version
variables.doc: The server version string, for example 8.4.2 or 11.4.3-MariaDB.

variables.name: @@version_comment
variables.doc: The server build description, such as MySQL Community Server - GPL.

variables.name: @@hostname
variables.doc: The name of the host the server runs on.

variables.name: @@port
variables.doc: The TCP port the server listens on.

variables.name: @@datadir
variables.doc: The directory where the server keeps its data files.

variables.name: @@basedir
variables.doc: The directory the server is installed in.

variables.name: @@tmpdir
variables.doc: The directory the server uses for temporary files.

variables.name: @@time_zone
variables.doc: The session time zone, as SYSTEM, an offset such as +00:00, or a named zone.

variables.name: @@system_time_zone
variables.doc: The time zone of the host operating system when the server started.

variables.name: @@character_set_server
variables.doc: The server's default character set for new databases.

variables.name: @@character_set_database
variables.doc: The character set of the current default database.

variables.name: @@character_set_client
variables.doc: The character set of statements sent by this client.

variables.name: @@character_set_connection
variables.doc: The character set used for literals that have no introducer.

variables.name: @@character_set_results
variables.doc: The character set the server uses when sending results to this client.

variables.name: @@collation_server
variables.doc: The server's default collation for new databases.

variables.name: @@collation_database
variables.doc: The collation of the current default database.

variables.name: @@collation_connection
variables.doc: The collation used for literals and comparisons in this connection.

variables.name: @@transaction_isolation
variables.doc: The transaction isolation level: READ-UNCOMMITTED, READ-COMMITTED, REPEATABLE-READ or SERIALIZABLE (MySQL; MariaDB 11.1+).

variables.name: @@tx_isolation
variables.doc: The transaction isolation level (MariaDB; removed in MySQL 8.0, use @@transaction_isolation).

variables.name: @@transaction_read_only
variables.doc: Whether new transactions are read-only (MySQL; MariaDB 11.1+).

variables.name: @@tx_read_only
variables.doc: Whether new transactions are read-only (MariaDB; removed in MySQL 8.0).

variables.name: @@read_only
variables.doc: Whether the server refuses writes from ordinary users (replicas usually set this).

variables.name: @@super_read_only
variables.doc: Whether the server refuses writes even from administrators (MySQL only).

variables.name: @@max_connections
variables.doc: The most client connections the server accepts at once.

variables.name: @@max_allowed_packet
variables.doc: The largest packet or generated string the server accepts, in bytes.

variables.name: @@wait_timeout
variables.doc: Seconds an idle non-interactive connection may sit before the server closes it.

variables.name: @@interactive_timeout
variables.doc: Seconds an idle interactive connection may sit before the server closes it.

variables.name: @@lock_wait_timeout
variables.doc: Seconds a statement waits for a metadata lock before failing.

variables.name: @@innodb_lock_wait_timeout
variables.doc: Seconds an InnoDB transaction waits for a row lock before giving up.

variables.name: @@innodb_buffer_pool_size
variables.doc: Bytes of memory InnoDB uses to cache table and index data.

variables.name: @@innodb_flush_log_at_trx_commit
variables.doc: How strictly InnoDB flushes its log at commit: 1 is fully durable, 0 and 2 trade durability for speed.

variables.name: @@default_storage_engine
variables.doc: The storage engine new tables use when none is named, usually InnoDB.

variables.name: @@auto_increment_increment
variables.doc: The step between successive AUTO_INCREMENT values.

variables.name: @@auto_increment_offset
variables.doc: The starting point for AUTO_INCREMENT values.

variables.name: @@foreign_key_checks
variables.doc: Whether foreign key constraints are enforced (1) or skipped (0) in this session.

variables.name: @@unique_checks
variables.doc: Whether InnoDB checks unique secondary indexes during bulk loads (1) or skips them (0).

variables.name: @@sql_safe_updates
variables.doc: When 1, UPDATE and DELETE without a key in WHERE or a LIMIT are refused.

variables.name: @@sql_select_limit
variables.doc: The most rows a SELECT returns when it has no LIMIT of its own.

variables.name: @@group_concat_max_len
variables.doc: The longest result GROUP_CONCAT returns, in bytes; longer results are cut.

variables.name: @@max_execution_time
variables.doc: Milliseconds a read-only SELECT may run before the server stops it; 0 means no limit (MySQL only).

variables.name: @@max_statement_time
variables.doc: Seconds any statement may run before the server stops it; 0 means no limit (MariaDB only).

variables.name: @@long_query_time
variables.doc: Seconds a query must take to be written to the slow query log.

variables.name: @@slow_query_log
variables.doc: Whether the slow query log is on.

variables.name: @@general_log
variables.doc: Whether every statement is written to the general query log.

variables.name: @@log_bin
variables.doc: Whether binary logging is on.

variables.name: @@binlog_format
variables.doc: The binary log format: ROW, STATEMENT or MIXED.

variables.name: @@server_id
variables.doc: This server's unique id within a replication topology.

variables.name: @@gtid_mode
variables.doc: Whether global transaction ids are used for replication (MySQL only).

variables.name: @@identity
variables.doc: The last AUTO_INCREMENT value inserted in this session; same as LAST_INSERT_ID().

variables.name: @@last_insert_id
variables.doc: The last AUTO_INCREMENT value inserted in this session; same as LAST_INSERT_ID().

variables.name: @@warning_count
variables.doc: How many warnings, errors and notes the last statement produced.

variables.name: @@error_count
variables.doc: How many errors the last statement produced.

variables.name: @@pseudo_thread_id
variables.doc: The connection id the server uses for temporary tables in this session.

variables.name: @@session.sql_mode
variables.doc: The SQL modes of this session only; @@global.sql_mode holds the server default.

variables.name: @@global.sql_mode
variables.doc: The server-wide default SQL modes for new sessions.

variables.name: @@session.time_zone
variables.doc: The time zone of this session only.

variables.name: @@global.time_zone
variables.doc: The server-wide default time zone for new sessions.
